clue.text: Good sign, mostly, about boys being happy once

indicators.note: about means the first pieces are wrapped around the boys
mostly means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: an omen is a sign of things to come
lads are boys

explanation.surface: A favourable omen about the boys makes everyone cheerful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts OMEN to OME; G and OME then go 'about' LADS.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic word for joyful or cheering, hence the 'once' marking it as old-fashioned.

clue.text: Weight reduced with a lot of skill and a system of rules

indicators.note: reduced means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a gramme is a unit of weight

indicators.note: a lot of means most of the word, the last letter dropped

parts.note: art is skill

explanation.surface: A trimmed weight and plenty of skill sounds like a recipe for a well-ordered system.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reduced' cuts GRAMME to GRAMM and 'a lot of' cuts ART to AR.
explanation.definitionFit: Language study treats syntax and morphology as a body of rules governing how words combine.

clue.text: Form of current around river bend

indicators.note: around means the current wraps the river

parts.note: AC, alternating current, is one form of electric current

explanation.surface: An electric current flows around a curve in a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A curve or curved line, as in a bow shape, is a synonym for a bend.

clue.text: Use standby shifts for special clothes

indicators.note: shifts means the letters move around into a new order

explanation.surface: Advice to wear a backup set of shifts, the dresses, on a special occasion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shifts' looks like a noun for dresses, but it is the anagram signal on USE STANDBY.
explanation.definitionFit: One's finest outfit, kept for church and occasions, is an idiom for special clothes.

clue.text: Satisfied about Biblical text in church music

indicators.note: about means the first word goes round the text

parts.note: met, as in met demands, means satisfied
OT is the Old Testament

explanation.surface: Someone content with a Bible passage set to choral music.
explanation.definitionFit: A short sacred choral composition, often unaccompanied, is a kind of church music.

clue.text: University location affected our team

parts.note: camp means affected or exaggerated in manner
us is our team, the group the speaker belongs to

explanation.surface: Something at the university has had an effect on our side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'affected' reads as a verb but is the adjective meaning theatrical, giving CAMP.
explanation.definitionFit: The grounds and buildings of a college are where a university is sited.

clue.text: Crack around top of head produces pain

indicators.note: around means the expert goes round the letter

parts.note: a crack shot is an ace, an expert

indicators.note: top of means the first letter, in this down clue the top one

explanation.surface: A cracked skull leads to pain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crack' looks like a fracture but means expert, ACE, which goes 'around' H.
explanation.definitionFit: A dull continuous hurt is a synonym for pain.

clue.text: In favour of striking after Government's initial brainwashing

indicators.note: after places the striking piece behind the Government letter

parts.note: pro means in favour of

indicators.note: initial means the first letter of the word

parts.note: ramming is striking forcefully

explanation.surface: Supporting a strike after a Government lead, perhaps through propaganda.
explanation.definitionFit: Conditioning someone's mind by repetition is a figurative sense matching brainwashing.

clue.text: The last crooks to display cunning

indicators.note: crooks, as a verb, means bends out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The final gang of criminals shows guile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crooks' reads as criminals, but as a verb it bends THE LAST into a new order.
explanation.definitionFit: Furtive, sly action is a sense shared with cunning in old usage.

clue.text: Half of team keen to bring in new youngster

indicators.note: half of means the first two of four letters
to bring in means the keen word holds the new letter

parts.note: eager is keen

explanation.surface: A team captain eager to recruit a young new player.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half of' takes two of the four letters of team; 'to bring in' sets the new letter in the middle of the keen word, not at an end.
explanation.definitionFit: Anyone aged thirteen to nineteen is a young person, an adolescent youngster.

clue.text: Take over kingdom, having others enchanted magically

indicators.note: magically means the letters are transformed as if by a spell

explanation.surface: A fairy-tale usurper bewitches rivals to seize a realm.
explanation.definitionFit: Becoming monarch is the idiom for assuming rule over a kingdom.

clue.text: Build at the sports ground and refuse to move?

definitions.meaning: construct a grandstand for spectators at a stadium

explanation.surface: Builders at a stadium dig in their heels.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally constructing spectator seating, and idiomatically taking a firm position of resistance.

clue.text: Criticises one on Times about supporting strike

indicators.note: on, in a down clue, places the one above the times sign
about means the criticising word goes around the supporting one

parts.note: knocks means criticises
for means supporting, as in for the motion
I is the Roman numeral one
X is the multiplication sign, times

explanation.surface: A critic of The Times backs a strike at the newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' is not the newspaper but the multiplication sign X; 'on' puts I above it.
explanation.definitionFit: To hit someone for six, a cricket shot clearing the boundary, means to strike or devastate them; cricket is England's summer bat-and-ball sport.

clue.text: Feature of reef failing first examination

indicators.note: failing first means the word loses its opening letter

parts.note: coral makes up a reef

explanation.surface: A marine biology student flunks the first exam about reefs.
explanation.definitionFit: A spoken test, as in a viva, is a kind of examination.

clue.text: Line retained by company actor not having a common attachment to line

indicators.note: retained by means the line letter sits inside the company abbreviation
not having means the word drops the letter a

parts.note: a thespian is an actor

explanation.surface: A theatre company keeps an actor's line, though without a usual attachment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'line' at the end is the washing line, not a line of dialogue.
explanation.definitionFit: A peg fixing laundry to a washing line is the commonest thing clipped to one.

clue.text: Greek character recalled problem about British diamond

parts.note: rho is a letter of the Greek alphabet

indicators.note: about means the reversed problem goes round the British letter
recalled means the word is called back, read backwards

parts.note: a sum is an arithmetic problem

explanation.surface: A Greek man remembers a problem about a British diamond.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' turns SUM into MUS, which goes 'about' B.
explanation.definitionFit: A parallelogram with four equal sides is the geometric name for a diamond shape.

clue.text: Characteristic events on the radio offended religious centre

indicators.note: on the radio means the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: sinned means offended, in the moral sense
Rome is the centre of the Catholic church

explanation.surface: A radio broadcast upset the Vatican.
explanation.definitionFit: A set of symptoms occurring together is a medical pattern of characteristic events.

clue.text: Girl's beginning to use speed in run, though clumsily

parts.note: gal is a girl

indicators.note: beginning to means the first letter of the following word

parts.note: mph, miles per hour, measures speed

explanation.surface: A girl starts to pick up speed in a run, if awkwardly.
explanation.definitionFit: Lewis Carroll's coinage for moving in a heavy, ungainly way is to lumber or run clumsily.

clue.text: Appreciates the money earned by Pole at home

parts.note: the take is the money taken, the takings
S is the south pole
in means at home

explanation.surface: A Polish worker brings home his earnings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' looks like a Polish person but is a magnetic pole, S.
explanation.definitionFit: To absorb or understand something fully is a phrasal-verb sense of appreciating it.

clue.text: French city bringing in one million for vacations etc.

indicators.note: bringing in means the city holds the next pieces

parts.note: Tours is a city on the Loire
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A French city attracts a million holidaymakers.
explanation.definitionFit: Travel for pleasure, holidays and sightseeing, is the industry built on vacations.

clue.text: Skirt needing attention around back: not true?

indicators.note: back means the whole is read backwards
around means the attention word goes round the skirt

parts.note: ear means attention, as in lend an ear
a kilt is a skirt

explanation.surface: A skirt in need of attention round the back is not quite right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' wraps the skirt in the attention word and 'back' then turns the whole result over. A rat is slang for a traitor, hence 'not true'.
explanation.definitionFit: Traitors are called rats, so behaving like one is being disloyal, not true to friends.

clue.text: Group he left to engage in economics

indicators.note: to engage in means the next pieces go inside economics

parts.note: econ is a short form of economics

explanation.surface: A man quits a job to take up economics.
explanation.definitionFit: A rank or level within an organisation is a stratum or group.

clue.text: Some inhabitants of Uranus taking a spin in these?

definitions.text: Some inhabitants of Uranus taking a spin in these?

indicators.note: taking a spin means the letters turn round, read backwards
some means only part of the words is used

explanation.surface: Aliens from Uranus might go for a whirl in flying saucers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' picks SOFU from 'inhabitantS OF Uranus', and 'taking a spin' turns it around.
explanation.definitionFit: Unidentified flying objects, flying saucers, are what aliens would travel in.

clue.text: Munitions left by English — not quite the safe distance?

indicators.note: by sets the English piece beside the left letter

parts.note: arms are munitions

indicators.note: not quite means the word drops its last letter

explanation.surface: Weapons abandoned by the English, but not quite at a safe distance.
explanation.definitionFit: Keeping something as far away as an outstretched limb is an idiom for a safe distance.

clue.text: Greek characters will be revealed in this dawn

parts.note: the answer split as an instruction, a word followed by up, turned over in a down clue gives NUS, two Greek letters nu

explanation.surface: A promise that Greek letters will be revealed at daybreak.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: read the answer as SUN then 'up', and in a down light SUN going up reads NUS, the plural of the Greek letter nu.
explanation.definitionFit: The moment the sun rises is daybreak, the dawn.

clue.text: Origin of tattoo? Daughter having booze

parts.note: rum is a kind of booze

explanation.surface: A daughter's drinking led to her getting a tattoo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tattoo' is not ink on skin but a drumbeat, as in a military tattoo.
explanation.definitionFit: A tattoo is a rhythmic beat, so the percussion instrument beating it is its source.

clue.text: Unusual sunlamp with Internet control system

indicators.note: unusual means the letters are arranged in an uncommon way

explanation.surface: An odd sunlamp operated over the Internet.
explanation.definitionFit: The dashboard of dials and switches in a car or aircraft is a control system.

clue.text: Endlessly queue up, getting nothing for it!

indicators.note: up, in a down clue, means the letters are read from bottom to top
endlessly means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a line is a queue

explanation.surface: An endless wait in a queue, getting nothing for one's patience.
explanation.definitionFit: Zero, especially as a sports score, is a synonym for nothing.

clue.text: Heads of military alliance backed a shuffle in top positions

indicators.note: heads of means the first letters of the next words
backed means the pieces are read backwards

parts.note: to mix is to shuffle

explanation.surface: Military chiefs back a reshuffle of top posts.
explanation.definitionFit: The plural of the Latin word for greatest values: peaks or top positions.

clue.text: Old writer, not elaborate, omitting one description of office

parts.note: a pen is a writer, the instrument

indicators.note: omitting means the word drops the one

parts.note: plain means not elaborate
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An old author writes simply, leaving something out.
explanation.definitionFit: An office without partition walls is described by this layout term.
